ios.expected: Re-running the repro: both commands exit 1 within a second with `Error: Invalid argument: Flow file not found: missing.yaml` (wording free, must name the path), and nothing is booted, built or installed (no `Booting` line). • `--flow` naming a directory, or an unreadable file, fails the same way. • Configured flows in grantiva.yml that do not exist fail the same way before boot (check whether config loading already covers it; if not, include it). • No failure screenshot for this error. • GrantivaCLITests/RunCommandTests: `run --flow <missing>` with a fake device platform throws before `bootDevice` is called (assert the fake recorded no boot). (brief K44 Acceptance criteria; Platforms: both)

ios.command: brief K53: MCP build, simulator and emulator tools report failures as JSON-RPC internal errors instead of `isError` results
ios.precondition: MCP: iOS `grantiva_build` failing, `grantiva_sim_boot {name: "no-such-sim"}`; Android `grantiva_emulator_boot`/`grantiva_emulator_delete` "no-such-avd" and a hand-made (avdmanager, never booted) AVD with and without `force: true`
ios.expected: Re-running the repro: every call answers `{"result":{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"Error: ..."}],"isError":true}}`; no response carries `"error"`. Cancellation still propagates as cancellation. • The hand-made-AVD refusal says `Pass force: true to delete it anyway.` (or names the argument) in the MCP result; the CLI keeps `--force`. • `ToolRegistry.call` converts any thrown non-cancellation error from any tool into an isError result in one place (the existing `errorResult`). • GrantivaMCPTests/ToolErrorContractTests: with fakes that throw, `grantiva_build`, `grantiva_run`, `grantiva_sim_boot`, `grantiva_sim_delete`, `grantiva_emulator_boot`, `grantiva_emulator_delete`, `grantiva_emulator_ensure` and `grantiva_emulator_list` each return `isError == true` from `ToolRegistry.call` (none throws). (brief K53 Acceptance criteria; Platforms: both)

ios.command: brief K56: `grantiva_context` shows an empty app ID (and driver port 0 on Android) for a keep-alive runner session
ios.expected: `grantiva run --keep-alive` records the app ID it launched in the owner sidecar; `loadActiveSession` fills `bundleId` from it. Re-running the repro: `bundle_id: com.kylebrowning.Landmarks` (Android: `application_id: com.kylebrowning.landmarks`). • Android: `driver_port` shows the port the attached driver uses, or the line reads `driver_port: (forwarded on attach)`; never a bare `0`. • A sidecar written by an older Grantiva without the app ID prints `bundle_id: (unknown)`, not an empty value. • GrantivaCoreTests/KeepAliveSessionStoreTests: owner sidecar round-trips the app ID; GrantivaMCPTests/ContextToolTests: a keep-alive-derived session renders the app ID and no empty value lines. (brief K56 Acceptance criteria; Platforms: both)

ios.command: brief K57: The MCP server announces a hierarchy change after UI tool calls that failed and changed nothing
ios.precondition: `runner start --detach`; MCP failing `grantiva_tap`, rejected call, `resources/subscribe`, successful tap; grep `resources/updated`
ios.expected: Re-running the repro: no `notifications/resources/updated` for ids 1 and 2; one for id 4 (after the subscribe). • Without a `resources/subscribe`, no `resources/updated` notification is sent (or docs/mcp.md says notifications are sent to every client, if that is the intended contract). • A script whose first steps ran and a later step failed still notifies (the UI changed). • GrantivaMCPTests/SessionLifecycleTests (or UIToolsTests) with a fake server/notifier: an isError `grantiva_tap` and a rejected `grantiva_script` send no notification; a successful tap sends one. (brief K57 Acceptance criteria; Platforms: both)

ios.command: brief K67: Two concurrent `simulator ensure` calls for one new name make one device, but the second call fails trying to boot it again
ios.precondition: two concurrent `simulator ensure --name "cov2-ios-3 Race iPhone 17"`; count created simulators; delete
ios.expected: Re-running the repro: in 5 of 5 iterations both calls exit 0, print the same UDID on stdout, one stderr line says `Created …` and the other `Reused …`; `simctl list` shows one device. • While one call waits for its twin's boot, it does not print `Waiting for simulator capacity (n/max)` when n is below the limit; if it says anything, the line names the device and that another Grantiva process is booting it. • The capacity record for the device ends `active` with `bootedByGrantiva: true` (`simulator sessions --json`). • GrantivaCoreTests/SimulatorManagerTests: with an injected executor whose device list flips from Shutdown to Booted while `reserve` waits, `boot` issues no `simctl boot` and returns the booted device. • GrantivaCoreTests/SimulatorCapacityTests: a `pending` record for the same UDID held by another live pid, under the limit, yields a wait outcome distinct from "host full" (and the message helper renders it differently). (brief K67 Acceptance criteria; Platforms: ios)

ios.command: brief K68: `simulator teardown --udid <free UDID> --force --json` reports `reclaimed: true` when nothing held the device
ios.expected: Re-running the repro: `"reclaimed": false`, `"leaseReleased": false`, `processes: []`, exit 0; the text form prints `No processes were holding <udid>.` and no `Released the simulator lease` line. • After `kill -9` of a `run --keep-alive` (IOS-016 setup), `teardown --udid --force --json` reports `reclaimed: true` (the orphaned WDA/diagnose are reaped); `leaseReleased` is true only if the runner still held the lease when teardown ran (K79: the runner exits with its killed parent, so `leaseReleased: false` is correct). • `leaseReleased` is true only when the lease was held: its flock is held by another process, or the file carries a live (non-stale) claim such as a `runner start` hand-off. • GrantivaCoreTests/SimulatorLeaseTests: `forceRelease` on an unlocked lock file with an empty claim returns false; with the flock held by a child process, or with a live hand-off claim, it returns true and the next `acquire` succeeds. • GrantivaCoreTests/SimulatorReaperTests: a forced teardown with no processes and only a stale lock file yields `reclaimed == false`. (brief K68 Acceptance criteria; Platforms: ios) (corrected round 3)

ios.command: brief K69: `simulator teardown --udid` without `--force` leaves the device's runner home behind when the device has no capacity record
ios.precondition: `run` on a session-less simulator; `simulator teardown --udid --json`; device homes under `versions/*/devices/`
ios.expected: Re-running the repro: `teardown --udid "$UDID"` (no `--force`) removes `<runner home>/versions/*/devices/<udid>` for every installed runner version and exits 0; with `--json` the output says which homes were removed even when no session record existed (an outcome entry with `deviceHomesRemoved`, or a documented equivalent). • A home that cannot be removed makes teardown exit non-zero and name it (README:92), as the `--force` path does. • The device itself is not shut down or deleted (it was not booted or created by Grantiva). • GrantivaCoreTests/SimulatorManagerTests: `teardown(udid:)` with no capacity record and an existing device home in a temp runner home removes the home and reports it. (brief K69 Acceptance criteria; Platforms: ios)

ios.command: brief K70: A run with no `GRANTIVA_SESSION_ID` is refused on a simulator a named session owns; the README does not say so, and the message uses "Teardown" as a verb
ios.precondition: simulator ensured under `GRANTIVA_SESSION_ID=cov2-k70`; `run` with another/no session ID
ios.expected: README (host-policy paragraph, README:449-455) states that a simulator booted under a named `GRANTIVA_SESSION_ID` is reserved for that session: a run with another or no session ID is refused, and how to use it anyway (set the same `GRANTIVA_SESSION_ID`, or end the session with `grantiva simulator teardown --session-id <id>`). • The refusal reads, for example: `Simulator cov-ios-1 (<udid>) belongs to Grantiva session cov-ios. Run with GRANTIVA_SESSION_ID=cov-ios, end that session with `grantiva simulator teardown --session-id cov-ios`, or select another simulator.` No "Teardown" as a verb. • If the team decides instead that a session-less run may use such a device without taking a slot, the run in the repro passes and `simulator sessions --json` is unchanged; README states that. • GrantivaCoreTests/SimulatorCapacityTests: the refusal text for a foreign-session record contains `grantiva simulator teardown --session-id <id>` and `GRANTIVA_SESSION_ID=<id>`. (brief K70 Acceptance criteria; Platforms: ios)

ios.command: brief K71: The "No scheme specified" error tells `build build` users to pass `--app-file`, an option `build build` does not have
ios.precondition: project without a resolvable scheme: `build build --simulator <udid>`; with `--app-file x.app`
ios.expected: `build build` with no scheme (one or several detected): the message offers `--scheme` and `scheme:` in grantiva.yml only, plus the `Found: …` list when several schemes exist. • `build install`, `run` and `diff capture` still mention `--app-file`. • The MCP `grantiva_build` / `grantiva_run` text is unaffected or follows the same rule (no CLI flag names there). • GrantivaCoreTests/ProjectResolutionTests (or GrantivaCLITests/BuildCommandTests): resolving without a scheme for a caller that cannot take a pre-built binary yields a message without `--app-file`; for one that can, with it. (brief K71 Acceptance criteria; Platforms: ios)

ios.command: brief K72: A cached one-scheme detection keeps picking that scheme silently after the project gains a second scheme
ios.precondition: `build build --derived-data-path dd` twice, second time after adding a second scheme
ios.expected: Re-running the repro: the last `build build` exits non-zero with `No scheme specified … Found: Landmarks, Landmarks (UI Testing).` • A one-scheme project still auto-detects silently, on first and on cached runs. • The cache cannot supply a scheme when no scheme is configured unless it is known to match the current project (either re-detect in that case, or invalidate the cache when the `.xcodeproj`/`.xcworkspace` scheme set changes). • GrantivaCoreTests/ProjectResolutionTests: a cached `DetectedProject` with `schemes: ["A"]` plus a detector that now reports `["A", "B"]` and no configured scheme throws the no-scheme error naming both. (brief K72 Acceptance criteria; Platforms: ios)

ios.command: brief K73: `build install --bundle-id <other>` fails with a raw simctl `No such file or directory` instead of naming the bundle ID mismatch
ios.expected: Re-running the repro: exit non-zero before or right after install with a message naming both IDs, for example `--bundle-id com.example.Other does not match the built app (com.kylebrowning.Landmarks, …/Landmarks.app/Info.plist).` No `NSPOSIXErrorDomain` text. • With a matching `--bundle-id` (or none) the command behaves as today (IOS-022/IOS-023). • If the team prefers to keep installing and only fail the container lookup, the lookup failure is mapped to `com.example.Other is not installed on <simulator>` plus the installed app's ID. • GrantivaCLITests/InstallCommandTests: an injected platform whose product Info.plist says `A` and `--bundle-id B` produces the mismatch error and never calls the data-container lookup with `B`. (brief K73 Acceptance criteria; Platforms: ios)

ios.command: brief K74: iOS `launchApp: {arguments: …}` also sends every argument as a launch environment variable named after the flag
ios.precondition: `run --no-build --flow ... --report-dir out`; launch body and argv in the runner log under `out/`
ios.expected: Decision recorded: either arguments are argv only, or the mirroring is kept and documented (README:172/176). • If argv only: re-running the repro shows `env=map[]` for that launch and a launch body without `environment` (or without the `--flag` key); `argv=["--flag" "true"]` is unchanged and flow 10-lifecycle still passes on 26.0 and 27.0. An app that relied on `ProcessInfo.environment["--flag"]` needs `environment:` instead: say so in the release notes. • If kept: README says `arguments:` keys are also set as environment variables on iOS, and the matrix row is corrected. • Runner test (pkg/driver/wda): `launchApp` with `Arguments{"--flag": true}` and no `Environment` sends a launch request whose environment lacks `--flag` (or, if kept, asserts the documented behaviour). • Bundled runner version bumped in this repo if the runner changes. (brief K74 Acceptance criteria; Platforms: ios)

ios.command: brief K75: iOS `swipe … from:` on a missing element says `Element not found:` without "for swipe", unlike the Android drivers
ios.precondition: `run --no-build --flow ...` on cov2-ios-1 and cov2-ios-2; the `✗ swipe` message
ios.expected: iOS 26.0 and 27.0: the swipe step fails with a line beginning `Element not found for swipe:` that names `text='No Such Row'` (the closest-texts cause may follow); exit 1. • The off-screen variant keeps its own wording (`Element is off-screen (not missing): …`) but also says it was for a swipe. • Android (UIAutomator2 and devicelab) also name the selector, so both platforms print the same structure (coordinate with whoever owns AND-219 / K01-style step wording). • Runner tests: WDA `swipe` with a `From` selector that matches nothing returns a message containing `for swipe` and the selector description; same for the UIAutomator2 driver. • Bundled runner version bumped in this repo if the runner changes. (brief K75 Acceptance criteria; Platforms: ios)

ios.command: brief K76-a: A passing step that took 5 s or longer is drawn with the warning glyph `⚠` and no reason, so it reads as a warned step
ios.precondition: `run --no-build --flow ... --report-dir out`; slow passed step lines, no `⚠`
ios.expected: Re-running the repro: the wait step prints `✓ extendedWaitUntil: notVisible text="Loading…" (5.2s)` (duration may stay yellow); the summary block likewise. • A slow passed step never prints `⚠` unless it also carries a warning; if a slow marker is kept, it is a different token that says what it means (for example `✓ … (32.4s, slow)`), in colour and without colour. • A warned step (e.g. an inputText whose typed value was replaced) still prints `⚠` followed by `╰─ warning: <reason>`. • Runner tests (pkg/cli): rendering a passed command with `Duration >= slowThresholdMs` and empty `Warning` produces `✓`; with a non-empty `Warning` produces `⚠` plus the warning line; both for the live, summary and nested paths. • Bundled runner version bumped in this repo. (brief K76-a Acceptance criteria; Platforms: both)

ios.command: brief K76-b: iOS `scrollUntilVisible` takes 32-36 s to reach a row about 70 items down, roughly 2 s per scroll
ios.expected: The runner log of the repro shows, per iteration, the find, scroll and settle durations (debug level is enough), so the cost is measured rather than guessed. • Each `scrollUntilVisible` in 08-scroll completes in at most half of today's time on iOS 26.0 and 27.0 (≤ 17 s per search; adjust the target once the timeline is known and record it in the fix PR), still finding both elements and passing the flow. • The fast path does not regress the "half-hidden element" and "made no progress" behaviours (commands.go:792-810, :823-825). • Runner test (pkg/driver/wda, fake client): a miss in the per-iteration find does not block for the step's full find timeout when the element is absent from the tree, and settle takes at most N screenshots on a static screen. • Bundled runner version bumped in this repo. (brief K76-b Acceptance criteria; Platforms: ios)

ios.command: brief K77: iOS `launchApp: {clearState: true}` clears the app's data but nothing in the run output or the runner log says so
ios.expected: Re-running the repro: the runner log has an Info line for the step such as `[wda] clearState com.kylebrowning.Landmarks: uninstalled and reinstalled from <staged path> (0.8s)`; a failure logs which half failed. • With `--verbose` the run output shows that line (or the step line reads `launchApp (clearState)` and the launch result message mentions the clearing). • Behaviour unchanged: the marker file is gone, the flow passes on 26.0 and 27.0, and 10-lifecycle still passes. • Runner test (pkg/driver/wda): `launchApp` with `ClearState: true` on a simulator driver records a log entry (or result message) for the clear. • Android: check the UIAutomator2 `clearState` path and add the equivalent line if it is silent too. • Bundled runner version bumped in this repo. (brief K77 Acceptance criteria; Platforms: ios)

ios.command: brief K78: MCP `grantiva_tap {label: "heart"}` taps the Favorites tab through its SF Symbol identifier
ios.expected: Contract chosen and written in docs/mcp.md:50 (and the tool description in Sources/GrantivaMCP/Tools/UITools.swift): label only, or label then identifier. • If label only: re-running the repro, id 3 returns `isError: true` with `Element not found: "heart". Run grantiva hierarchy (or the grantiva_a11y_tree MCP tool) to inspect the tree.`; id 2 still taps Favorites and returns its tree; `grantiva_script` `{"tap": "heart"}` fails the same way. • If the fallback stays: the result says how it matched (for example `Tapped on "heart" (matched by identifier)`), docs/mcp.md says so, and matrix row IOS-102 is corrected. • GrantivaCoreTests/WDAClientTests: with a stub server where `label == "heart"` returns 404 and `name == "heart"` returns an element, `tapByLabel("heart")` throws `elementNotFound` (label-only) or reports the identifier match (fallback). (brief K78 Acceptance criteria; Platforms: ios)

ios.command: brief K79: After `kill -9` of a keep-alive `grantiva run`, its runner lives on and `hierarchy` keeps serving the dead run's session
ios.precondition: `run --keep-alive`, `kill -9` of that grantiva pid (one this row started), then `hierarchy --timeout 10`, runner pid state; `runner start --detach` control
ios.expected: Re-running the repro: after `kill -9` of the `grantiva run` pid, `grantiva hierarchy` exits non-zero within a second with the no-session error (or names the orphaned runner and the reclaim command `grantiva simulator teardown --udid <udid> --force`); it never prints the tree. • Either the orphaned runner exits on its own when its parent dies (and removes its session file), or every reader (`hierarchy`, `runner dump-hierarchy`, MCP session lookup) ignores a `run --keep-alive` session whose owning grantiva pid is dead. • `runner start --detach` sessions keep working after the starting process exits (`hierarchy`, `runner dump-hierarchy` and MCP tools still attach). • docs/dump-hierarchy.md:21 matches the behaviour. • GrantivaCoreTests/KeepAliveSessionStoreTests: a runner file with a live runner pid and an owner whose `grantivaPid` is dead (and which is not a `runner start` owner) is excluded from `liveSessions()`; a `runner start` owner with a dead starter pid is included. (brief K79 Acceptance criteria; Platforms: ios)

ios.command: brief K80: After a `--timeout` kill, the `--report-dir` report.json still says the run and its flow are `running`
ios.precondition: `run --no-build --flow ... --timeout 30 --report-dir out`; report status of the killed flow
ios.expected: Re-running the repro: report.json has `"status": "failed"`, `summary.running: 0`, `summary.failed: 1`, and the flow's status `failed` with an error saying grantiva stopped it at the `--timeout` cap; flow-000.json agrees; the JUnit file records one failure (or is rewritten consistently). • The ready file is unchanged (`failed`, flow `failed`, `reportDir` set because `--report-dir` was given). • The same holds for the screens path (`diff capture` / configured screens with `--timeout`, IOS-135) and for an interrupt (`kill -INT` → `interrupted` in both files). • GrantivaCoreTests/RunnerSessionReportTests (or RunnerReportWorkspaceTests): given a report dir whose report.json says `running`, the timeout finaliser rewrites it to `failed` with no `running` flows. (brief K80 Acceptance criteria; Platforms: ios)

ios.command: brief K81: `--snapshot trailing` trims only the `captures/trace/` copy; the report directory still keeps before and after shots of every step
ios.precondition: `run --no-build --flow ... --snapshot trailing --report-dir out`; count shots in assets/ and allure-results/
ios.expected: Re-running the repro: the report directory holds, besides `captures/failure-*.png`, only the last good step's `after` and the failing step's shots (in `assets/flow-000/` and wherever else the report references them), and report.json / allure references no deleted file. • `--snapshot full` still keeps every step; `--snapshot failure` keeps only the failure shot. • Without `--report-dir` the visible result (`captures/trace/`) is unchanged. • GrantivaCoreTests/RunnerTraceExportTests: a fixture report dir with before/after for steps 0-2 and a failure at step 2, trimmed in `trailing` mode, leaves `cmd-001-after`, `cmd-002-before`, `cmd-002-after` in `assets/` and updates or drops the report references to the removed files. (brief K81 Acceptance criteria; Platforms: ios)

ios.command: brief K82-a: `run --snapshot full` (and `trailing`) reports every per-step trace shot as a captured screen and copies it into `captures/`
ios.precondition: `run --no-build --flow ... --snapshot full --report-dir out`; the `Screens:` line and screenshot list
ios.expected: Re-running the repro: `Screens: 2 total, 2 passed, 0 failed`; `captures/` holds the two takeScreenshot captures (plus `trace/` with the step shots); no `-before`/`-after` file outside `trace/`. • `--snapshot trailing` likewise lists only takeScreenshot points. • The collector identifies named screenshots from report.json (the takeScreenshot command's artifact) rather than by globbing, or excludes the runner's `cmd-NNN-before\|after.png` names. • GrantivaCoreTests/RunnerArtifactCollectorTests: a fixture `assets/flow-000/` with `cmd-000-before.png`, `cmd-000-after.png` and `cmd-003-Home.png` yields exactly one capture, `01-browse-cmd-003-Home`. (brief K82-a Acceptance criteria; Platforms: ios)

ios.command: brief K82-b: `run` leaves its takeScreenshot shots and failure screenshots in `.grantiva/captures`, and `diff approve`/`diff compare` then treat them as screens
ios.precondition: `run` without `--report-dir` (pass and fail); `ls .grantiva/captures .grantiva/run-captures`; then `diff approve`/`diff compare`
ios.expected: Re-running the repro: `diff approve` approves exactly the 5 configured screens; `diff compare` compares exactly those; no `failure-*` or `01-browse-cmd-*` baseline is written. • Either `run` writes its captures and failure shots somewhere `diff` does not read (for example `.grantiva/runs/<ts>/`), or `diff capture` records a manifest (or clears stale files) and approve/compare use only the manifest. Whatever is chosen, README (`--snapshot`, failure screenshot, `diff approve`) says where each kind of file goes. • Existing baselines named like old run artifacts are not silently deleted; at most a note lists them. • GrantivaCLITests/DiffCommandTests: a capture directory with configured screens plus `failure-1.png` and `flow-cmd-003-Home.png` approves and compares only the configured screens. (brief K82-b Acceptance criteria; Platforms: ios)

ios.command: brief K83: A `takeScreenshot` inside a `runFlow` sub-flow runs but never becomes a capture point
ios.expected: Re-running the repro: `Captured 2 screens`, `FromSub.png` and `Main.png` in `.grantiva/captures/`, in that order; same with `runFlow: {file: sub.yaml}`. • A cycle or missing sub-flow still fails with the existing errors; a sub-flow with no takeScreenshot adds no screen. • Duplicate names across parent and sub-flow are reported as an error (or disambiguated) rather than overwriting. • GrantivaCoreTests/MaestroStandardFormsTests (or a new MaestroFlowParser test): parsing the two files above yields screens `["FromSub", "Main"]`. (brief K83 Acceptance criteria; Platforms: ios)

ios.command: brief K84: `record --frames-at` with a timestamp past `--duration` records the full duration and overwrites the previous video before failing
ios.expected: Re-running the repro: the second command exits 64 in well under a second with a message such as `--frames-at 5000 is past --duration 2 (2000 ms).`; no recording is started and the previous `recording.mov` is unchanged. • A timestamp equal to `duration × 1000` is accepted; a recording that ends slightly short of a valid timestamp still gets today's post-recording error. • GrantivaCLITests/RecordCommandTests: `--duration 2 --frames-at 5000` fails `validate()` (or fails before the injected device's `recordVideo` is called), and `--duration 2 --frames-at 2000` passes validation. (brief K84 Acceptance criteria; Platforms: ios)

ios.command: brief K85: `record --json` gives `video` as a relative path and every frame `path` as an absolute one
ios.precondition: `record --duration 3 --frames-at 0,1000` with relative and absolute `--output`, text and `--json`
ios.expected: Re-running the repro: `video` and every `frames[].path` use the same style. Pick one for the CLI (relative to the current directory when the output was given relatively, as `diff capture --json` does, or absolute everywhere) and apply it to the text output too. • An absolute `--output` gives absolute paths throughout. • GrantivaCLITests/RecordCommandTests: with an injected device and a relative `--output`, the encoded report's `video` and frame `path`s are all relative (or all absolute, per the chosen rule). (brief K85 Acceptance criteria; Platforms: ios)

ios.command: brief K86-a: A simulator held by `runner start` is refused as "another Grantiva run … --keep-alive" and the advice omits `grantiva runner stop`
ios.precondition: `runner start --detach` on the device, then `run --no-build --flow ...` on it; the refusal text; a `run --keep-alive` owner as control
ios.expected: Re-running the repro: exit 1 fast, session intact, and the message names the owner as a `runner start` session, for example `Simulator <udid> is held by a `grantiva runner start` session (grantiva-runner pid 52144, started 58s ago). Stop it with `grantiva runner stop` (from <project dir>), or use another simulator via `grantiva simulator ensure --name <unique-name>`.` • A `run --keep-alive` owner keeps today's wording, and a dead owner still suggests `teardown --force`. • The Android emulator variant gets the same distinction. • GrantivaCoreTests/SimulatorLeaseTests: `ownershipMessage` for a handed-off claim mentions `grantiva runner stop` and not `--keep-alive`; for a keep-alive run claim it is unchanged. (brief K86-a Acceptance criteria; Platforms: ios)

ios.command: brief K86-b: `diff capture --no-build` picks the live `runner start` session's simulator, then refuses to run on it
ios.precondition: `runner start --detach`, then `diff capture --no-build` from the same dir (captures through the session); a `runFlow` screen fails asking for `grantiva runner stop`
ios.expected: One of: - Capture through the session: re-running the repro, `diff capture --no-build` captures the 5 screens on the session's simulator through the live runner (as `grantiva_vrt_capture` does), exit 0, and the session is still usable afterwards (`grantiva runner dump-hierarchy` answers); or - Drop the tier: the session's device is no longer chosen implicitly; with several booted simulators the command fails naming them (README order without the session step), and with the session's device as the only booted one it fails up front with `grantiva runner stop` advice instead of resolving then refusing. README:262-264 updated. • GrantivaCLITests/DiffCommandTests: with an injected live session and no flag/config simulator, `noBuildDevice` (or its replacement) either returns a session-backed target or throws the documented message before any runner spawn. (brief K86-b Acceptance criteria; Platforms: ios)

ios.command: brief K87: `runner stop` sometimes leaves the runner's own `<pid>-<ts>.grantiva` session file in /tmp/grantiva-sessions
ios.precondition: 10 cycles of `runner start --detach` / `runner dump-hierarchy` / `runner stop`; `ls /tmp/grantiva-sessions` after each
ios.expected: Re-running the repro: no cycle leaves a `<pid>-*.grantiva` for the stopped pid (10 of 10). • `runner stop` removes the stopped runner's session file itself once the process is gone (for example via `KeepAliveSessionStore().removeSessions(udid:runnerPids:[pid])`), and gives the runner enough time to release WDA before escalating, or reports when it had to SIGKILL. • GrantivaCLITests/RunnerLifecycleCommandTests: `RunnerStopCommand.run(dependencies:)` with a fake runner that ignores SIGINT calls the session-file cleanup for that pid. (brief K87 Acceptance criteria; Platforms: ios)

android.command: brief K76-a: A passing step that took 5 s or longer is drawn with the warning glyph `⚠` and no reason, so it reads as a warned step

android.command: brief K79: After `kill -9` of a keep-alive `grantiva run`, its runner lives on and `hierarchy` keeps serving the dead run's session

android.command: brief K81: `--snapshot trailing` trims only the `captures/trace/` copy; the report directory still keeps before and after shots of every step

android.command: brief K82-b: `run` leaves its takeScreenshot shots and failure screenshots in `.grantiva/captures`, and `diff approve`/`diff compare` then treat them as screens

android.command: brief K111: Android `record --duration 4` can write a 6.16 s video: a screenrecord overrun is never trimmed

(brief K111 Acceptance criteria; Platforms: android) K111 is open (not fixed in the round-2 fix wave): record the measured track lengths and grade `fail` unless the track ends at `--duration` (plan N2-01).

android.command: brief L01: Android inputText fails on the fixed 10 s HTTP timeout of the key-actions request even though the text was typed
android.precondition: 3 x `run --no-build --flow .maestro/03-edit.yaml --report-dir r$i` alone on `cov2-android` (`emulator ensure` defaults, software rendering; record `hw.gpu.*` from its config.ini), then the stock set; the `inputText " Renamed"` step duration
android.expected: On a software-rendered API 35 AVD (`emulator ensure` defaults, `hw.gpu.mode` resolving to lavapipe), 03-edit passes 3 of 3 runs alone and inside the stock set (12/12 with 10-seed-many per L03), and `inputText " Renamed"` finishes within the step timeout. • A request that is still in progress when a fixed transport deadline would have expired is governed by the step's deadline instead (context from the step, or a per-request timeout at least the remaining step time); no UIAutomator2 call is cut at a hard-coded 10 s while its step still has time. • If the key-actions request does time out, the runner reads the focused field; when it holds the expected `before + text`, the step passes (optionally with a note that the server answered late); otherwise it fails naming UIAutomator2 and the timeout, without repeating the cause. • Typing does not grow linearly into the timeout: either chunk long text into several `/actions` requests or size the deadline from the character count; an 8-character append on the slow AVD takes well under the step timeout. • Runner tests: pkg/uiautomator2 — a fake server that answers `/actions` after 12 s with a 30 s step context succeeds, and one that never answers fails at the step deadline, not at 10 s. pkg/driver/uiautomator2 (next to input_append_test.go) — `SendKeyActions` returns a timeout error but the fake field then reads "Golden Gate Bridge Renamed": `inputText` succeeds; the field still reads "Golden Gate Bridge": it fails. (brief L01 Acceptance criteria, docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-12-coverage-issues-round2/ on coverage-campaign e27f0a4; Platforms: android)

android.command: brief L02: On Android a find request blocked against a crashing app stalls the crash check for 10 s, and assertVisible then passes on the dead app
android.precondition: 3 x `/usr/bin/time -p grantiva run --no-build --flow .maestro/99-crash.yaml --report-dir r$i` on `cov2-android`; step and wall times, `error.type`
android.expected: 99-crash on the default `emulator ensure` AVD fails 3 of 3 at `launchApp` or the first step after it (never passes a step; round 3 ruling: cold `launchApp` waits for the first frame, so the crash usually lands there; AND-107 correction), with `error.type` `app_crash` and the `LANDMARKS_CRASH_ON_LAUNCH` cause, within ~2 s of the process dying (assert step under ~3 s; flow and wall time back near round 1: flow < 6 s, wall < 12 s on that AVD). • The crash check runs concurrently with an in-flight find request (or the request is bounded by the next crash-poll tick through a context), so a request blocked by a dying app cannot delay crash detection beyond one `crashPoll`. • The first attempt of an element wait is covered when the watch is armed and the find did not return promptly. • No element-wait step reports success while the launched process is gone with a FATAL EXCEPTION logged since launch: a match found after the process died is re-checked before the step passes. • Runner tests in pkg/driver/uiautomator2 (next to wait_crash_test.go / crash_test.go): a fake client whose first `FindElement` blocks 10 s while the fake device reports the process gone plus a FATAL EXCEPTION makes `assertVisible` fail with `ErrAppCrashed` within 2 s; a fake whose looser strategy then matches still fails with `app_crash`, not success. (brief L02 Acceptance criteria, docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-12-coverage-issues-round2/ on coverage-campaign e27f0a4; Platforms: android)
